actual_scope: Can some ports keep the hosted form while the others use the two-chain form, in one native word with one joint contact per stage, so that the complete signed invoice improves over the all two-chain word?
scope_change_reason: Same native construction, A6 declaration and BIT line as #6902. Changed: the root becomes a pair (type A: the two-chain root, 96 ports; type B: the hosted root of #6889, 8 ports), the caller is block diagonal over 78 roles with one stage value per stage and 18 joint contacts, and the word has 400 mains (the 8 hosted ports have no second mains), 59,918 events, 967 helpers. Correctness rests on the exact replay of the final word, the two root checkers and the block-diagonal caller replay. Owned registers read mains 16 times (8 of Y2, 7 of X, 1 of X2), peak 30, coefficient bits 13/10. Raw counts 962,308,192 / 968,225,044 / 978,594,376, all below 10^9; logarithm power minimum 2159, written 2160 (on the literal carrier 153; an earlier version used 145 and was too low). The BIT saving of the open #6726 (.00376669) is necessary. LAMBDA priced as ordinary work is a review question. Inherited: owned ascent (A6), LAMBDA and IDLE_ONE, the reducible type A root.
bottleneck_link: docs/research/research-family-status.md; complete signed native/caller invoice and all supplier-admission gates
stop_rule: The claim is conditional on the five retained framework assumptions, the declared owned ascent (A6), the BIT saving of the open #6726, and the declared forms (a per-port root, a reducible type A root, HOST2 and the joint contact, same-label second mains); no claim above the pin; LAMBDA must be priced as ordinary work for any crossing to exist.
